_note: DEFAULT-DENY allowance for the skip gate (tests/skip_gate.py). Every skip reason that occurs, whatever its wording, must appear here with its exact count; there is no allow-list of 'known' wordings. classify()/COMPILE_ENV_PATTERNS only label the log lines and name which reasons the 'engine_built' profile pins at 0. Keys are the EXACT skip reason text (a renamed reason is drift too). 'default' is the profile the engine-less hosted-CI pytest job runs; its counts are the WHOLE skip population of the measured run (2,358 skips across 13 reasons), not only the compile-environment ones. 'engine_built' is the profile the engine-building CI job runs: the compile-environment reasons are pinned at 0 so any such skip fails that job; see _engine_built_note.
_measured_on: 2026-10-11 spot box (Ubuntu 24.04, python 3.12), engine-less with NO PINEFORGE_* variables set; the counts are the WHOLE skip population of that run (2,358 skips across 13 reasons), not only the compile-environment skips
_engine_built_note: UNMEASURED. The engine-building CI job runs this profile, but the counts below are NOT a measurement of that job: they are copies of the engine-less `default` run and are EXPECTED to be WRONG. That job now DOES set PINEFORGE_ENGINE_CORPUS, cloning the public pineforge-4pass/pineforge-corpus at b40aa8ecbe3caa9ad05244cdfd9ee8138da845e4 (the gitlink the pinned engine commit 4e01e96b5165b5d5e46d72bfbbf88ae6c035a6e9 records), so its corpus tests DO run. It does NOT set PINEFORGE_STRING_SETTINGS_SOURCES, because the population sources that variable would point at are NOT public: this repository carries no fixture for them and the public corpus checkout above has no file matching the sha12 names the test globs, so its six population-source cases skip -- hence that row is 6, not 0. Expect the FIRST engine-built run to FAIL on the other rows and the gate to print the exact rows to write here; paste those rows in to measure this profile. The compile-environment rows (the 'PINEFORGE_ENGINE_INCLUDE not set or invalid...' and 'set PINEFORGE_ENGINE_INCLUDE...' rows, 'engine include / compiler unavailable', 'set PINEFORGE_ENGINE_INCLUDE plus a valid pineforge-engine corpus checkout...', 'PINEFORGE_ENGINE_CORPUS is needed for emitted-byte comparison', 'input receipt corpus pin requires PINEFORGE_ENGINE_CORPUS') must stay 0: building the engine and pinning the public corpus must remove every one.

engine_built._note: engine_built is kept for a MANUAL single-job run; the CI jobs now run the engine_built_shard_<i> profiles, one per leg of the `engine-shard` matrix, so this profile is not the one they run.

engine_built_shard_0._note: UNMEASURED: engine_built_shard_0 is the profile the `engine-shard` matrix job runs for shard 0 of 10. It is a COPY of the `engine_built` profile (the compile-environment reasons at 0, every other reason at its engine_built count) and is EXPECTED to be wrong: a shard runs only its own hash slice of the collected test files, so a reason whose tests all land in another shard is counted in neither direction here. The compile-environment rows ('PINEFORGE_ENGINE_INCLUDE not set or invalid...', 'set PINEFORGE_ENGINE_INCLUDE...', 'engine include / compiler unavailable', 'set PINEFORGE_ENGINE_INCLUDE plus a valid pineforge-engine corpus checkout...', 'PINEFORGE_ENGINE_CORPUS is needed for emitted-byte comparison', 'input receipt corpus pin requires PINEFORGE_ENGINE_CORPUS') are 0 because the shard extracts the built engine and the pinned public corpus from the `engine-env` artifact, which removes every one. The shard's FIRST run prints the exact rows to paste in; replace the copied counts with those rows and set _unmeasured per profile to false when done. The 'population sources require PINEFORGE_STRING_SETTINGS_SOURCES' row stays at 6, its `engine_built` value: that knob's sources are not public, so the skip is real and the artifact cannot close it (see `_engine_built_note`).
